item.title: Semgrep benchmarks show GLM 5.2 outperforms Claude Code in IDOR vulnerability detection with 39% F1 score versus 32%, using open-weight model from Zhipu AI [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Semgrep's recent benchmarks reveal that GLM 5.2, an open-weight model from Zhipu AI, outperforms Claude Code in detecting Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR) vulnerabilities, achieving a 39% F1 score compared to Claude Code's 32%. This evaluation used the same dataset and prompt across models, highlighting GLM 5.2's competitive edge despite lacking the specialized harness that boosts Semgrep's own multimodal pipeline to 53-61% F1. GLM 5.2 stands out due to its open-weight availability under an MIT license, allowing security teams to run and fine-tune it internally. It features a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 750 billion parameters and supports extended context lengths up to one million tokens, which is beneficial for complex security tasks. Additionally, its cost efficiency is notable, operating at roughly one-sixth the price of comparable frontier models. These factors make GLM 5.2 a promising option for AI-driven vulnerability detection in security workflows.

item.title: Brown University professor reports mass AI cheating by at least 50 students on March midterm exam in advanced economics course [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Professor Roberto Serrano of Brown University has uncovered widespread cheating involving artificial intelligence by at least 50 students during the March midterm exam in his advanced economics course. This incident represents the largest known academic integrity breach at Brown and across the Ivy League. Despite presenting conclusive evidence, Serrano reported receiving minimal response from university leadership, prompting calls for a more serious and transparent approach to addressing AI-related cheating. The course, which traditionally enrolls fewer students, saw an unusual increase to 86 participants this semester, likely due to a new take-home exam format. The midterm results were unusually high, with many answers matching AI-generated content. In response, the final exam was held in person, resulting in significantly lower scores and attendance. Serrano emphasizes the need for open discussion and stronger measures to uphold academic standards in the face of evolving AI challenges.

item.title: User employs Claude Code with Opus 4.8 to analyze MRI results, finds AI diagnosis contradicts human report on shoulder tendon tear [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A user with shoulder pain used Opus 4.8 within Claude Code to analyze their MRI results and obtain a second opinion on a diagnosis of a partial-thickness tear in the subscapularis tendon. The AI analysis contradicted the human medical report by finding the tendon intact, prompting further comparison between the two assessments. The AI arbiter favored the AI reader's conclusion, identifying mild tendinosis but no tear, raising questions about the initial diagnosis and treatment plan. The user detailed their experience setting up the AI analysis, including providing limited clinical context and allowing the AI to install necessary packages for MRI data processing. They also noted concerns about the original treatment, such as the use of shockwave therapy and homeopathic injections, which were flagged by another AI model. Despite the AI's decisive verdict, the user remains uncertain about fully trusting AI over human experts and is considering further medical consultation or continued rehabilitation. This case highlights the potential and current limitations of AI in medical diagnostics, illustrating how AI can challenge traditional diagnoses but also create uncertainty for patients. It underscores the need for cautious integration of AI tools in healthcare and the importance of expert oversight in interpreting AI-generated findings.

item.title: Researchers introduce Proxy-KD method to improve knowledge distillation from black-box large language models, outperforming traditional white-box techniques [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Proxy-KD, a new method to improve knowledge distillation from black-box large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4. This approach uses a proxy model to facilitate effective knowledge transfer to smaller models, overcoming the challenge of inaccessible internal states in proprietary LLMs. Experiments demonstrate that Proxy-KD not only enhances distillation from black-box teachers but also outperforms traditional white-box techniques. The Proxy-KD method offers a promising solution for leveraging the capabilities of advanced LLMs without requiring access to their internal mechanisms. This advancement could accelerate the development of smaller, more efficient models that retain high performance by learning from powerful but opaque teacher models.

item.title: OpenAI Codex issue to add file exclusion mechanism for sensitive data remains open as of June 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: An open issue on OpenAI Codex's GitHub repository highlights the need for a feature that allows users to exclude sensitive files from being read or sent to the model. This mechanism would enable explicit marking of files or paths to be ignored at both repository and global levels, such as .env or .ssh directories, to protect sensitive data and improve security. The proposal suggests a deterministic and shareable configuration system, like a .codexignore file, that can be used across teams and projects. Although a related issue was previously closed in favor of a Rust implementation, as of mid-2026, no equivalent feature exists, prompting renewed discussion and interest in developing this functionality.

item.title: Researchers propose DysLexLens, a low-resource LLM framework analyzing dyslexic learners' AI tool experiences via Reddit forums with dictionary filtering and knowledge-graph reasoning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DysLexLens, a low-resource large language model (LLM) framework designed to analyze the experiences of dyslexic learners using AI tools by examining discussions on Reddit forums. The framework transforms noisy social media posts into a focused corpus using dictionary-driven filtering, applies knowledge-graph-based reasoning for semantic analysis, and generates verifiable responses that are evaluated through both quantitative metrics and human assessment. DysLexLens features four main components: a filtering method to improve data relevance, integration of LLM-assisted semantic analysis with knowledge-graph query reasoning, quantitative evaluation metrics to assess response quality, and structured guidelines for qualitative validation focusing on hallucination and evidence alignment. The framework was tested on dyslexia-related Reddit data with 30 questions, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential applicability to other low-resource online forum contexts. The researchers have made DysLexLens, along with sample data and evaluation results, publicly available on GitHub to support reproducibility.

item.title: Researchers argue that the term machine unlearning is overused in large language model research and should be reserved for dataset-defined deletion with retraining equivalence guarantees [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers argue that the term "machine unlearning" is often misapplied in large language model (LLM) research and should be specifically reserved for the process of dataset-defined deletion. This involves removing the influence of a precisely specified subset of training data so that the resulting model closely resembles one retrained without that data. They highlight that many current uses of "unlearning"-such as refusal of harmful requests or targeted knowledge suppression-serve different, policy-driven goals and thus require distinct terminology and evaluation methods. The paper emphasizes that conflating these different objectives under the same label leads to confusion and misuse of metrics and benchmarks, which may reward superficial indicators rather than true retraining equivalence. The authors call for clearer terminology tied to explicit guarantees and reference models, along with evaluations that align with the specific objectives claimed by each approach.

item.title: Researchers release Supersede, a reinforcement-learning environment to diagnose and train memory-update gaps in LLM agents, improving fact currency accuracy from 9.0% to 16.7% on real conversations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Supersede, a reinforcement-learning environment designed to address the challenge of memory-update gaps in large language model (LLM) agents during long, multi-session interactions where facts change over time. Their study reveals that even advanced models like GPT-5.4 experience significant accuracy drops when relying on bounded, self-maintained memory instead of full context, highlighting a persistent issue in memory maintenance rather than comprehension. Supersede rewards agents for using current facts and penalizes outdated information, providing a novel training signal to improve temporal fact accuracy. Testing Supersede with a smaller open model, Qwen2.5-3B, demonstrated that fine-tuning nearly doubled the model's accuracy in handling updated facts during real conversations, increasing from 9.0% to 16.7%. This marks the first evidence that the supersession gap-difficulty in updating and maintaining current facts-can be effectively trained down rather than merely measured. The environment and findings offer a new approach to enhancing LLM agents' ability to manage evolving information in dynamic conversational settings.

item.title: Researchers introduce MMEE corpus and benchmark speech emphasis models across 7 languages and 34 emotions, finding multilingual training improves robustness and cross-emotion transfer is strong [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the MMEE (Multilingual Multi-Emotion Emphasis) corpus, comprising 10,000 professionally recorded expressive utterances across seven languages and 34 emotion or style categories, to study prosodic emphasis in speech. They evaluated two advanced speech emphasis detection models under various conditions, including monolingual, cross-lingual, multilingual, and cross-emotion settings, revealing that multilingual training enhances model robustness compared to monolingual approaches, which struggle with zero-shot transfer especially across typologically distant languages. The study found that models transfer effectively between high- and low-arousal emotions and that there is a shared prosodic structure between synthetic and perceptual benchmarks, as indicated by bidirectional transfer. Additionally, the models maintained strong performance even with smaller training datasets, suggesting potential for efficient training across diverse linguistic and emotional contexts.

item.title: Researchers propose Smooth Maximum Mean Discrepancy (SMMD) to improve numerical prediction accuracy in large language models across mathematical and visual tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Smooth Maximum Mean Discrepancy (SMMD), a novel training objective designed to enhance the numerical precision of large language models (LLMs). Unlike standard cross-entropy loss, which treats numeric tokens as unrelated categories, SMMD incorporates value-distance kernels and graph-based smoothness to better align predicted numeric distributions with target values. This approach addresses the challenge of LLMs producing unreliable outputs when exact numerical accuracy is required. The team evaluated SMMD across four tasks involving numeric targets-mathematical reasoning, arithmetic calculation, clock-time recognition, and chart question answering-using various open-weight LLM and vision-language model backbones. Results showed consistent improvements in accuracy over traditional cross-entropy and recent numeric-target loss functions. Analyses highlighted the complementary benefits of combining maximum mean discrepancy with smoothness and emphasized the importance of designing distance-based kernels. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration.

item.title: Researchers introduce VASAE, a vocabulary-aligned sparse autoencoder that assigns intrinsic token names to Transformer features without reducing reconstruction quality, aligning about 90% of features in GPT-2-small layers 0-10 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Vocabulary-Aligned Sparse Autoencoder (VASAE), a method that trains sparse autoencoder features to align directly with a Transformer's token vocabulary by assigning each feature an intrinsic token name based on the nearest token embedding. VASAE maintains reconstruction quality comparable to standard sparse autoencoders while producing dictionaries with vocabulary-aligned features, achieving about 90% alignment in GPT-2-small layers 0 to 10 and strong alignment in shallow and middle layers of Llama-3.1-8B. The study shows that after adjusting for sentence-level mean sparse codes, many intrinsic token names correspond closely to nearby input tokens, suggesting that vocabulary-aligned anchoring effectively connects learned features to token identities during training. This approach complements traditional post hoc interpretations of learned dictionaries and enhances understanding of Transformer residual stream decompositions.

item.title: Researchers propose MultiHashFormer, a hash-based generative language model framework enabling autoregression with constant parameter footprint, outperforming standard Transformers at 100M to 3B scales [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MultiHashFormer, a novel hash-based generative language model framework that enables autoregressive processing with a constant parameter footprint. Unlike traditional language models that use large embedding matrices scaling with vocabulary size, MultiHashFormer represents each token as a unique hash signature composed of multiple discrete hash IDs. This approach allows the model to compress token representations efficiently and generate the next token's hash signature, which is then decoded back to text. The team evaluated MultiHashFormer at parameter scales of 100 million, 1 billion, and 3 billion, finding that it consistently outperforms standard Transformer language models across various benchmarks. Additionally, the model supports multilingual vocabulary expansion without increasing its parameter footprint or requiring modifications, highlighting its scalability and efficiency for diverse language tasks.

item.title: arXiv:2606.28127 argues large language models are a special case of world models with a continuous spectrum from token prediction to latent-space architectures, examining data and architecture challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The paper on arXiv titled "From Tokens to States: LLMs as a Special Case of World Models and the Continuous Path Beyond" challenges the common view that large language models (LLMs) and world models are fundamentally different. It argues that LLMs are a specific, limited form of world models where the state space consists of token sequences and actions involve appending tokens. The authors propose a continuous spectrum of models bridging token prediction and latent-space architectures, with intermediate approaches like multi-token and future-summary prediction already explored in current research. The paper also discusses two key challenges in advancing beyond traditional LLMs: the availability of large-scale self-supervised data versus the need for instrumented, action-labeled environments, and whether transformer architectures can generalize to continuous-state prediction or if new model primitives are necessary. These issues highlight open research questions about data sources and architectural design in the pursuit of more general intelligence models.

item.title: Researchers introduce Epi2Diff framework using LLM reasoning traces to predict human item difficulty with interpretable cognitive episodes, outperforming baselines on four datasets including SAT benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Epi2Diff, a novel framework that uses reasoning traces from large language models (LLMs) to predict human item difficulty in educational assessments. By converting LLM reasoning into cognitively meaningful episodes, Epi2Diff models difficulty based on problem-solving effort and state transitions, offering an interpretable approach beyond traditional text-based methods. The framework outperforms existing baselines across four datasets, including SAT benchmarks, demonstrating an 8.1% average relative improvement over supervised LLM fine-tuning. Epi2Diff groups segments of reasoning traces into functional problem-solving states, capturing dynamics such as reasoning scale and effort allocation. Experiments reveal that more difficult items trigger more complex and iterative cognitive episodes rather than simply longer responses. This approach provides a scalable and interpretable process representation for understanding item difficulty, potentially enhancing fairness and effectiveness in educational measurement.

item.title: Google introduces Paper Assistant Tool to automate scientific peer review, improving error detection by 34% and piloting at STOC and ICML conferences [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google has developed the Paper Assistant Tool (PAT), an AI-powered system designed to automate and enhance the scientific peer review process. PAT analyzes full scientific manuscripts to evaluate theoretical results, validate experiments, suggest improvements, and detect potential errors, achieving a 34% improvement in identifying mathematical errors compared to previous methods. The tool has been piloted at major computer science conferences, including STOC and ICML, where it has successfully identified critical issues and helped improve research papers before submission. By integrating PAT into the review workflow, Google aims to address the growing challenge of scaling traditional peer review to keep pace with the rapid increase in AI-assisted scientific research. The tool reduces the cognitive load on human reviewers while maintaining their oversight, potentially accelerating the verification and publication of scientific findings.

item.title: Researchers introduce LiveClawBench, a benchmark with 134 executable cases across 10 domains to evaluate LLM agents on complex, real-world assistant tasks with stateful execution [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced LiveClawBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents on complex, real-world assistant tasks that require stateful execution. The benchmark addresses the challenge of fidelity in evaluation by combining a Triple-Axis Complexity Framework for task difficulty with reproducible full-stack mock applications that maintain execution semantics. LiveClawBench includes 134 executable cases across 10 domains and 22 mocked services, enabling controlled and extensible assessment of realistic agent behaviors. LiveClawBench overcomes limitations of existing benchmarks, which often simplify task distributions or environments, by preserving real-world complexities such as cross-service dependencies, contaminated state, implicit intent, and runtime changes. The benchmark resources, including the benchmark itself, a leaderboard, and task trajectories, have been made publicly available to support further research and development in LLM-based personal assistants.

item.title: Researchers propose Embedded Language Flows, a continuous diffusion model in embedding space that outperforms discrete and continuous diffusion language models with fewer sampling steps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Embedded Language Flows (ELF), a new class of continuous diffusion models for language generation that operate primarily in continuous embedding space before mapping to discrete tokens at the final step. This approach, based on continuous-time Flow Matching, allows ELF to leverage techniques from image-domain diffusion models and achieve superior generation quality with fewer sampling steps compared to existing discrete and continuous diffusion language models. ELF's design minimizes adaptations needed for discrete language data, enabling effective continuous diffusion modeling in language tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that ELF outperforms leading diffusion language models, suggesting it as a promising direction for advancing continuous diffusion approaches in natural language processing.

item.title: Researchers propose Student-Centric Answer Sampling to improve LLM training by selecting teacher answers based on student learning cost rather than teacher strength alone [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Student-Centric Answer Sampling (SCAS), a new approach to training large language models (LLMs) that selects teacher-generated answers based on the estimated learning cost for the student rather than relying solely on the teacher's overall performance. This method challenges the common practice of using the highest-performing teacher as the best source of supervision, demonstrating that the strongest teacher's answers are not always the most effective for every student model. SCAS uses a token-wise gradient decomposition to estimate a student-centric learning cost and guides answer selection during training accordingly. Experiments involving 30 teacher models, 6 student models, and 6 tasks showed that SCAS consistently improves student performance, suggesting that tailoring supervision to the student's current state can enhance the effectiveness of knowledge distillation in LLM training.

item.title: Reference MCP launches tool enabling AI agents to search each other's past sessions across multiple platforms locally and offline [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Reference MCP is a local, offline tool that allows AI agents to search and access each other's past session transcripts and memory files across multiple platforms. By integrating with tools like Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Cursor, it enables seamless cross-tool collaboration and information retrieval without data leaving the user's machine. The tool operates through a single MCP server that reads session data from various AI tools on the user's device, using a lightweight BM25 ranking system for efficient search. It supports easy setup with minimal dependencies and is extensible to additional tools via simple configuration, enhancing AI agents' ability to recall and reference previous interactions across different environments.

item.title: Natural 20 discusses navigating AI challenges and opportunities with ethical considerations and skill development amid rapid technological change [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article explores the challenges and opportunities brought by rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, emphasizing the importance of ethical considerations and skill development. It advises professionals to navigate AI's evolving landscape thoughtfully, avoiding burnout and maintaining critical thinking rather than relying solely on AI tools. The author highlights that no one has fully mastered AI yet, and cautions against blaming AI for broader industry issues, encouraging users to leverage AI to enhance their abilities rather than outsource their expertise. The discussion includes practical perspectives on how to engage with AI constructively, such as questioning AI decisions and using it as a collaborative partner to accelerate learning. The article underscores the need for a balanced approach to AI adoption amid ongoing technological change, suggesting that those who actively own their learning process will be better positioned for future success despite uncertainties in the market.

item.title: Natural 20 forecasts five key shifts in the future of work driven by AI delegation, command literacy, and changes in labor structure [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The article presents five key forecasts about the future of work, emphasizing a fundamental shift driven by AI delegation, command literacy, and changes in labor structures. It argues that work itself-not just jobs-is being transformed as AI becomes more capable and integrated, shifting from a tool for information retrieval to an agent for task execution. This transition redefines how humans interact with AI, moving from asking questions to assigning work orders, which will reshape organizational practices and labor economics. The forecasts highlight that the traditional model of scaling work by increasing headcount will evolve as AI agents take on substantial work blocks. The article stresses the importance of new skills such as command literacy, delegation, and objective-setting, which will become critical for workers to effectively manage AI-driven labor. This shift is expected to impact various sectors beyond software, including finance, law, sales, and marketing, signaling a broad restructuring of how work is organized and measured in the future.

item.title: Researchers introduce ODYSSEY, a categorical framework for constructing verifiable local truth-preserving foundation models using composable foundries, with full implementation and testing across diverse domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ODYSSEY, a categorical framework designed to construct verifiable, local truth-preserving foundation models through compositions of modular components called foundries. These foundries organize knowledge with built-in argumentation and cover various domains such as evidence, decision-making, finance, and scientific research. The framework employs Universal Foundry Learning to formalize foundry construction using advanced mathematical tools, and Foundry SQL to query and integrate external models securely. ODYSSEY has been fully implemented and tested across diverse concrete foundries, demonstrating its capability to support domain construction, artifact management, diagnostic analysis, and causal claim extraction from heterogeneous sources. This comprehensive approach ensures robust verification and local truth preservation in foundation models. The research will be presented as a tutorial at ICML 2026, highlighting its significance for advancing trustworthy AI model development.

item.title: Researchers propose SD-GPS, a solver-driven framework combining autoformalization and verified theorem proposing to improve geometry problem solving with neuro-symbolic methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SD-GPS, a solver-driven framework designed to enhance geometry problem solving by integrating neural and symbolic methods. This approach addresses key limitations in current systems by linking the symbolic solver directly to both the autoformalization and theorem proving stages, improving compatibility and overcoming deductive impasses. SD-GPS combines supervised learning and reinforcement learning for formal language adaptation and employs an impasse-aware agent to propose verified auxiliary lemmas, ensuring soundness through symbolic verification. Evaluations on benchmark datasets Geometry3K and PGPS9K show that SD-GPS outperforms existing large language models and neuro-symbolic methods across various problem-solving tasks. By closing the loop between multimodal perception and symbolic execution, this framework significantly advances geometric reasoning and demonstrates how neural agents can be grounded in formal systems to achieve verifiable and effective problem-solving capabilities.

item.title: Researchers introduce Lifted Causal Inference algorithm using parametric causal factor graphs to speed up causal effect computation in relational domains with partial causal knowledge support [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Lifted Causal Inference (LCI) algorithm, which uses parametric causal factor graphs (PCFGs) to efficiently compute causal effects in relational domains. This approach leverages lifted inference to speed up causal effect computation by representing indistinguishable objects collectively, maintaining exact results while improving performance compared to traditional propositional methods like causal Bayesian networks. The team also introduced partially directed PCFGs (PD-PCFGs) to handle scenarios with partial causal knowledge, broadening the applicability of lifted causal inference to models with less prior causal information.

item.title: Researchers propose OverFlowLight, a real-time traffic signal control framework that reduces urban intersection gridlock by 60.4% and increases throughput by 18.2% across 43 intersections in three cities [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed OverFlowLight, a real-time traffic signal control framework designed to prevent gridlock at urban intersections by addressing queue overflow, a common cause of severe congestion. Tested across 43 intersections in three cities, OverFlowLight reduces overflow incidents by 60.4% and increases traffic throughput by 18.2% compared to existing systems. The framework uses multi-modal sensing from cameras and radars to detect overflow and dynamically adjusts signal phases to clear blocked queues, combining rapid rule-based interventions with reinforcement learning for improved efficiency. The system integrates seamlessly with current reinforcement learning-based traffic controllers, demonstrating modularity and practical applicability. By significantly reducing the need for manual adjustments typical of expert-tuned signal plans, OverFlowLight offers a scalable, data-driven solution to enhance urban traffic management and prevent cascading gridlocks, contributing to more resilient and efficient transportation networks.

item.title: Researchers release CalBrief, a pilot benchmark evaluating large language models' ability to generate evidence-calibrated scientific briefings across 16 evidence packages and 96 verified takeaways [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CalBrief, a pilot benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' (LLMs) ability to generate scientific briefings that accurately reflect the strength and scope of supporting evidence. The benchmark includes 16 diverse scientific evidence packages and 96 human-verified takeaways, using an auditable framework to identify where LLMs struggle in evidence calibration. The study found that while structured organization improves reasoning about roles and gaps in evidence, explicit strength-calibration policies tend to be overly conservative compared to baseline models. The research involved testing three closed-model backbones-GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet, and Gemini Flash-to diagnose causes of conservatism in strength calibration. Results showed that expanding the label space from binary to a four-way classification accounted for most of the conservatism, while other factors had minimal impact. Additionally, the study revealed that four-way predictions could be simplified back to binary labels without loss of information, indicating that nuanced labels carry valuable insights. The findings highlight a tension between label-level strength judgment and auditable evidence organization, suggesting these capabilities should be evaluated separately in LLM research assistants.

item.title: Researchers introduce DMV-Bench, the first interactive benchmark for multimodal agent visual memory using incidental cue injection in a 1,000-product e-commerce catalog [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced DMV-Bench, the first interactive benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal agents' visual memory in an environment where agents must recall visual information rather than relying on text. Built on a controlled e-commerce catalog of 1,000 home-furnishing products, DMV-Bench uses unique incidental visual cues embedded in product images to test an agent's ability to remember and navigate to specific items across multiple autonomous shopping sessions. The benchmark ensures that discriminative signals come solely from visual data, preventing text leakage. The team also proposed DualMem, a novel memory architecture inspired by dual-coding theory, which maintains parallel visual and verbal codes. DualMem outperformed existing multimodal agent-memory systems and a caption-based baseline across various task lengths on two different models, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Qwen2.5-VL-7B. The approach emphasizes visual cues for end-to-end memory while using verbal channels primarily for query grounding, demonstrating improved performance in long-horizon visual memory tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose LaViD framework transferring semantic knowledge from language-only large models to vision-only models, outperforming recent multimodal distillation methods on fine-grained benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LaViD, a framework that transfers semantic knowledge from large language models (LLMs) to vision-only models without relying on paired multimodal data. LaViD uses LLMs to generate multiple-choice questions that capture semantic distinctions between visual classes, creating soft label distributions that guide the vision model through an auxiliary distillation loss. This approach enables a language-only teacher model to effectively supervise a visual student model. LaViD outperforms recent multimodal distillation methods like MaKD and achieves competitive or superior results compared to state-of-the-art visual distillation techniques such as DKD and MLKD across multiple fine-grained benchmarks. It also enhances robustness to spurious correlations, as demonstrated by improved worst-group accuracy on the Waterbirds dataset. The framework's code has been made publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers introduce the context-ready transformer, a recurrent neural network architecture that pre-contextualizes tokens for faster generation and improved performance over standard transformers [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the context-ready transformer, a novel recurrent neural network architecture that enhances token processing by pre-contextualizing each token before it enters a transformer block. This approach uses a correction network to combine previous context with the current token embedding, enabling faster and more efficient left-to-right generation. The model can be trained by unrolling the correction process and can also be adapted from pretrained transformers through fine-tuning. Evaluations show that a five-layer context-ready transformer outperforms a 12-layer standard transformer while generating text 1.7 times faster on an A100 GPU. A single-layer version achieves a 2.6 times speedup over a six-layer transformer, with comparable performance in terms of perplexity. The architecture is particularly effective with wide representations and long contexts, and it demonstrates superior compositional abilities on tasks like pointer-chasing compared to standard transformers.

item.title: Researchers introduce MMG-Pop benchmark and MMG-PopNet model for multi-modal graph-based social media popularity prediction across Bluesky and Reddit datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MMG-Pop, a benchmark for multi-modal graph-based social media popularity prediction, along with MMG-PopNet, a unified model that integrates textual, visual, temporal, and social interaction signals. This work addresses fragmentation in existing studies by standardizing datasets, modalities, and evaluation protocols across platforms like Bluesky and Reddit. The new benchmark and model aim to improve the accuracy of forecasting online content reach and influence, which is crucial for applications such as advertising optimization and content strategy. MMG-Pop unifies multiple datasets and modalities under a consistent evaluation framework, while MMG-PopNet jointly models multi-modal signals and graph-structured social interactions. Experiments demonstrate MMG-PopNet's superior performance and provide insights into cross-platform generalization, multi-task prediction advantages, contributions of different modalities, and limitations of large language models in this context. These developments establish a foundation for future research on social dynamics modeling and intervention in complex, multi-modal social media environments.

item.title: Researchers prove perfect prompt-injection prevention is mathematically impossible in shared-embedding sequence models without architectural separation of instructions and data [ ~ ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that perfect prevention of prompt injection attacks in large language model (LLM) applications is mathematically impossible within shared-embedding sequence models that do not separate instructions from data. Their study formalizes these systems as Prompted Action Models and introduces the concept of Semantic-Faithful Control (SFC), which requires system behavior to depend solely on the meaning of untrusted input rather than its encoding. They prove that achieving SFC is unattainable due to inherent inseparability of trusted and untrusted content, exposure of control paths to untrusted tokens, and limitations of finite training data. The findings highlight structural vulnerabilities in current shared-embedding architectures, drawing parallels to longstanding security issues like buffer overflows in traditional computing. The researchers argue that no in-pipeline classification or alignment method alone can fully eliminate prompt injection risks. Instead, they conclude that architectural changes enforcing a clear separation between instruction and data channels are necessary to address this fundamental security challenge.

item.title: Researchers propose HIA-GAT, a heterogeneous graph attention network for frame-level traffic conflict risk prediction on freeways, achieving top risk-ranking performance on NGSIM I-80 and US-101 datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HIA-GAT, a heterogeneous graph attention network designed for frame-level traffic conflict risk prediction on freeways. This model treats risk assessment as a multi-agent scene graph classification task, using vehicles as nodes and modeling interactions through longitudinal and lateral edges enriched with physics-informed features. Tested on the NGSIM I-80 and US-101 datasets, HIA-GAT outperformed existing models in risk-ranking accuracy, particularly excelling in scenarios involving lane-change conflicts where relational structure is crucial. HIA-GAT employs a dual-stream attention mechanism to separately process longitudinal and lateral interactions, integrating them via a conflict-type-aware gating system supervised by conflict attribution data. This approach not only improves prediction accuracy but also offers interpretable insights into dominant conflict types per vehicle, enabling real-time, actionable freeway safety monitoring. The study highlights the importance of graph structures for modeling lateral conflict risks, while longitudinal risks can often be captured without relational modeling.

item.title: Researchers propose PEBS, a per-rater empirical-Bayes shrinkage method for RLHF reward-model calibration that reduces RMSE by up to 9.66% without retraining the base model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced PEBS, a per-rater empirical-Bayes shrinkage method designed to improve reward-model calibration in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). Unlike traditional approaches that use a single global calibrator for all annotators, PEBS fits individual affine calibrators for each rater and applies empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the population mean without retraining the base reward model. This method significantly reduces root mean square error (RMSE) by up to 9.66% on benchmark datasets, enhancing the accuracy of reward models by better accounting for individual annotator differences. PEBS operates as a closed-form, post-hoc estimator that adjusts annotator-specific calibration maps at inference time, leaving the underlying reward model unchanged. The approach was tested on the PRISM and PluriHarms datasets, demonstrating consistent RMSE improvements over the standard pooled population-slope baseline. This advancement offers a practical way to refine RLHF reward models by addressing systematic rating-scale variations among annotators, potentially leading to more reliable human feedback integration in reinforcement learning systems.

item.title: Researchers develop distribution-based deep multiple instance learning model for tumor proportion scoring in non-small cell lung cancer using slide-level labels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a novel deep multiple instance learning (MIL) model to improve tumor proportion scoring (TPS) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) using only slide-level labels. The approach combines an embedding-extraction and multiclass-classification network to capture histopathological features of tissue patches with a MIL model that predicts zero-inflated beta (ZIBeta) parameters representing the TPS probability distribution for entire slides. This distribution-based framework enhances prediction accuracy and explainability compared to traditional methods. The model addresses challenges such as the labor-intensive manual annotation of slides and the scarcity of certified experts by leveraging slide-level TPS scores without requiring detailed patch annotations. The ZIBeta modeling significantly outperforms baseline linear and ridge regression techniques, effectively handling non-expressive images and capturing expected accuracy through distribution concentration, demonstrating its potential for aiding treatment planning and prognosis in NSCLC.

item.title: Researchers introduce Retroactive Advantage Correction to reduce bias in delay-aware reinforcement learning from human feedback, improving policy accuracy by up to 47.9x in tests [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Retroactive Advantage Correction (RAC), a method designed to address delays in reward signals during reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). This approach queues and adjusts delayed feedback, reinjecting it into the learning process to correct bias caused by asynchronous rewards. Tests on a tabular Markov decision process showed that RAC can reduce policy bias by up to 47.9 times compared to existing methods, while also lowering computational costs. RAC works by applying a non-negative kernel to age pending feedback and reintegrate it as a clipped residual in subsequent optimization steps. The method is mathematically proven to be unbiased when all delayed feedback is accounted for and generalizes existing techniques like V-trace in the absence of delay. It integrates easily with popular reinforcement learning algorithms such as PPO and GRPO through minimal code changes. This advancement improves the accuracy and efficiency of RLHF systems that rely on slow or queued human or automated feedback, potentially enhancing the performance of AI models trained in real-world environments where immediate reward signals are not always available.

item.title: Researchers present Narrative-UFET, a method generating short narratives to improve ultra-fine entity typing on long-tail types by leveraging multi-sentence context [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Narrative-UFET, a novel approach to ultra-fine entity typing (UFET) that generates short, coherent narratives to provide multi-sentence context for entity mentions. This method addresses the challenge of accurately typing long-tail entities, which traditional sentence-level UFET methods struggle with due to limited contextual information. By pairing each entity with an automatically generated narrative, the researchers demonstrate improved performance, especially when the entity's type changes within the narrative, highlighting the value of extended discourse context. The study compares two narrative variants: one maintaining a constant entity type and another allowing type shifts, with the latter yielding stronger improvements over sentence-level baselines. Additionally, synthetic narratives outperform naturally occurring contexts, suggesting that controlled narrative construction can reveal implicit signals missed in real text. Despite these advances, the findings indicate significant opportunities for further research in discourse modeling and narrative generation to enhance entity typing accuracy.

item.title: Researchers introduce KARMA, a method using K-order Markov approximations to explain temporal dependencies in multivariate time series forecasting models, validated on real and synthetic data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed KARMA, a novel method that uses K-order Markov approximations to explain temporal dependencies in multivariate time series forecasting models. KARMA constructs a Markov surrogate model to capture the temporal relationships learned by the predictor, addressing the common limitation of existing explainable AI methods that assume timestamp features are independent. The approach identifies the minimal history length needed for accurate prediction, estimates the best-fitting Markov transition kernel, and provides a hierarchical global explanation framework, demonstrated on real-world weather data. The method was validated using complex synthetic data with known causal structures, showing that KARMA can recover the causal dependencies learned by the model more effectively than established attribution techniques like TimeSHAP. This advancement offers a more accurate and interpretable understanding of temporal dependencies in time series forecasting models, which is crucial for applications requiring sequential and causal consistency in explanations.

item.title: Researchers propose HybridCodec combining discrete tokens and continuous residuals for efficient speech language models, improving speaker characteristic retention and reducing autoregressive steps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HybridCodec, a new approach that combines discrete audio tokens with continuous residuals to enhance speech language models. This hybrid framework uses a discrete-continuous focal modulation codec alongside a hybrid Transformer, enabling efficient autoregressive inference in the discrete domain while applying non-autoregressive prediction and continuous residual upsampling. The method improves the preservation of speaker characteristics compared to discrete-only models and reduces the number of autoregressive steps needed. The approach addresses the common issue of information loss during audio discretization, which has previously led to performance degradation in multimodal text-audio systems and large language models. Experimental results demonstrate that HybridCodec effectively balances compression and detail retention, offering a promising direction for integrating audio capabilities into language models with improved efficiency and fidelity.

item.title: Researchers propose dual-threshold hard example mining to improve cross-platform Chinese offensive comment detection, demonstrating significant gains across Weibo, Xiaohongshu, Tieba, and Zhihu [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a dual-threshold hard example mining method to improve the detection of offensive comments across multiple Chinese social media platforms, including Weibo, Xiaohongshu, Tieba, and Zhihu. This approach addresses the common issue of performance degradation when deploying offensive comment detection models across different platforms by filtering error-prone samples based on prediction confidence and fine-tuning the model with a small set of manually labeled difficult examples. The method demonstrated significant performance improvements compared to baseline models under domain shifts. The study involved fine-tuning a RoBERTa model on a Chinese offensive language dataset to establish a baseline, followed by constructing a three-class fine-labeled test set spanning four platforms. The researchers quantified domain differences using metrics like Jaccard and Proxy-A Distance and identified bottlenecks in baseline performance. Their dual-threshold strategy selectively mines hard examples from unlabeled data, enabling low-cost cross-platform adaptation and enhancing detection accuracy in diverse social media contexts.

item.title: Researchers conduct factorised study of probe-based uncertainty estimation in large language models, finding structured features more robust under distribution shift and providing pretrained probes for factual generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have conducted a detailed study on probe-based uncertainty estimation (UE) methods used to detect hallucinations in large language models (LLMs). Their factorised analysis under controlled conditions reveals that while raw hidden states and attention features perform well within the same data domain, structured and compressed features demonstrate greater robustness when models face distribution shifts. The study also highlights the significant impact of prompting and label construction on probe behavior. Building on these insights, the team developed pretrained probes based on benchmark data that transfer effectively to open-ended factual generation tasks, offering a reliable baseline for uncertainty estimation. This work emphasizes the need for evaluation approaches that reflect real-world deployment scenarios and provides resources to support further research in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose Controlled Behavioral Divergence, an API-only black-box unlearning framework for large language models that improves unlearning utility and preserves model performance on similar data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Controlled Behavioral Divergence (CBD), a novel API-only black-box unlearning framework designed for large language models (LLMs). CBD addresses challenges in removing undesired data influence without retraining, especially when only API access is available and when unlearning target data closely resembles retained data. The framework uses auxiliary models to create behavioral divergence and routes unlearning-related prompts away from the target LLM, improving unlearning utility while preserving model performance. CBD enhances discrimination accuracy by constructing a gradient statistics-based discriminative basis, guiding unlearning signals toward target-specific information rather than shared prompt structures. Compared to eleven existing unlearning methods, CBD demonstrates superior trade-offs between unlearning effectiveness and utility retention, achieving near-retrained reference performance on benchmark tests while maintaining high accuracy on retained knowledge. The code for CBD is publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers propose preregistration protocol to mitigate p-hacking in LLM-based research by testing on the first eligible future model, blocking transfer of hacks in over 70% of cases [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a preregistration protocol to reduce p-hacking in studies involving large language models (LLMs). The protocol involves finalizing the experimental procedure on current models, preregistering the analysis plan along with a set of eligible future models, and then conducting the confirmatory analysis on the first eligible LLM released after preregistration. This approach prevents researchers from tuning parameters to achieve desired results on models that do not yet exist, as configurations that exploit one model often do not transfer to subsequent models. The protocol was tested on two tasks with known true values across 20 models from four providers and 11 analysis configurations. Results showed that it blocked successful transfer of p-hacking in approximately 73% of cases. Additional stress tests confirmed the robustness of the mitigation. The researchers also preregistered their own experiment following the protocol, which confirmed its effectiveness by preventing p-hacking transfer in 6 out of 7 configurations on the first eligible model released after preregistration.

item.title: Researchers find inference-time rollout rules impact accuracy and cost in multi-horizon volatility forecasting across 20 stock series and multiple model architectures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that in multi-horizon volatility forecasting for financial markets, the method used to deploy a trained model at inference time significantly affects both prediction accuracy and computational cost. By experimenting with different rollout rules on 20 stock-volatility series and various model architectures, including linear models and PatchTST, they observed that non-default deployment strategies often outperform the standard multi-output (MIMO) approach. However, the optimal rollout rule varies depending on the model and forecast horizon, making a single fixed strategy unreliable. To address this variability, the study evaluated validation-based deployment policies that select rollout rules dynamically. These policies improved performance under mean squared error (MSE) objectives while reducing inference costs compared to larger ensembles. The researchers also noted that the effectiveness of deployment policies depends on the evaluation metric, as strategies optimized for MSE did not consistently perform well under QLIKE, a common volatility loss measure in finance. The findings highlight the importance of considering deployment strategies alongside model architecture when assessing volatility forecasting methods.

item.title: Researchers present a meta-learning framework for anytime-valid certified robustness that reduces sample complexity 20-fold and enables adaptive compute allocation for real-time neural network certification [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a meta-learning framework that significantly improves the efficiency of Randomized Smoothing (RS), a method used to provide certified robustness guarantees for neural networks. Their approach reduces the sample complexity by a factor of 20 compared to traditional RS methods while maintaining rigorous statistical guarantees. This framework uses a lightweight meta-learner to predict image-specific priors, enabling adaptive allocation of computational resources during certification. Unlike standard RS, which requires a fixed and large number of model evaluations per input, this new method supports anytime-valid certification, allowing computation to be adjusted dynamically based on application-specific risk thresholds. This adaptive capability facilitates real-time, safety-critical deployments by enabling resource triage that was previously impossible under classic certification frameworks, all without compromising certification performance.

item.title: Researchers propose Class-frequency Guided noise schedule for diffusion models to improve generation quality on imbalanced datasets like CIFAR-100-LT and ImageNet-LT [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a Class-frequency Guided (CFRG) noise schedule for diffusion models to enhance generation quality on imbalanced datasets such as CIFAR-100-LT and ImageNet-LT. They identified that low-frequency classes suffer from inaccurately estimated scores due to large low-density regions, which leads to poorer sample quality and diversity compared to high-frequency classes. The CFRG noise schedule addresses this by assigning larger-scale noises to low-frequency classes, improving the balance in score estimation during the diffusion process. The team tested their approach across tasks including image generation, image classification, and text-to-image generation on imbalanced datasets. Their results showed significant improvements over baseline methods, highlighting the importance of incorporating class frequency statistics into the design of noise schedules for score-based generative models.

item.title: Researchers propose a certification-inspired dual-gate pipeline to reduce word error rate by up to 55% and enhance robustness in automatic speech recognition systems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a certification-inspired dual-gate pipeline to improve the robustness of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems, which are typically vulnerable to both adversarial and benign perturbations. This new approach significantly reduces the Word Error Rate (WER) by up to 55%, enhances recall, and lowers the correlation between confidence scores and errors, thereby improving the reliability of ASR outputs without requiring knowledge of the true transcription. The method involves a Two-Sided Atomic Audit that statistically certifies token existence and excludes adversarial interference, combined with a Rank-Based Tournament that selects the most accurate transcription sequence. Evaluations across four different ASR architectures demonstrate the effectiveness of this pipeline, which also provides detailed word- and sentence-level certifications to strengthen acoustic security and detection capabilities in deployed systems.

item.title: Researchers simulate over 8 million over-the-air acoustic attacks, showing up to 94.5% word error rate increase in Whisper and wav2vec voice recognition models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a high-throughput simulation framework to evaluate over 8 million over-the-air acoustic adversarial attacks on voice recognition models, revealing that such attacks can increase word error rates by up to 94.5% in systems like Whisper and wav2vec. This study addresses previous limitations by incorporating real-world acoustic factors such as detectability and environmental geometry, which were often overlooked in digital-only adversarial testing. The team introduced a Dual-Form Signal to Noise Ratio metric to separate the stealthiness of the attack source from its effectiveness on the victim system, enabling more precise assessment of attack risks. Their approach lays the foundation for reproducible and verifiable research that fully embraces the complexities of acoustic environments, improving understanding of vulnerabilities in voice-controlled AI systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce low-agreeableness persona conditioning to reduce jailbreak susceptibility and harmful outputs in large language model fine-tuning while preserving conversational warmth [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new fine-tuning method for large language models (LLMs) that reduces their vulnerability to jailbreaks and harmful outputs while maintaining conversational warmth. This approach involves conditioning user inputs on a low-agreeableness persona combined with warm, de-escalating assistant responses. Experiments across multiple models demonstrated that this technique lowers harmful output rates compared to traditional warmth fine-tuning methods, which often compromise factual reliability and safety. The study suggests that the increased susceptibility to adversarial attacks seen in warmth fine-tuned models may stem from data construction rather than an inherent trade-off with empathetic adaptation. By adjusting the training data to reflect low agreeableness in user turns, the researchers achieved safer empathetic fine-tuning without relying on safety labels, harm detectors, or changes to the training objectives. Representational analysis indicates this method reduces the alignment between warmth and compliance in the models' latent space, contributing to improved safety.

item.title: Researchers introduce The Simulacrum, a neural network framework using decision-theoretic pretraining for near-optimal time-series forecasting and inference with zero-shot capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed The Simulacrum, a neural network framework that uses decision-theoretic pretraining to create near-optimal estimators for time-series forecasting and inference. By training on simulations from a specified generative model and decision objective, the framework produces neural estimators capable of zero-shot inference on new time series, offering forecasts, parameter estimates, predictive intervals, and model selection. This approach directly targets finite-sample properties such as risk minimization, bias control, and calibration, enabling performance that surpasses traditional methods like maximum likelihood estimation and AICc-based model selection within the same model classes. The framework demonstrates competitive or state-of-the-art accuracy on real-world forecasting benchmarks, even when trained solely on simulated structural models. It addresses challenges such as finite-sample bias and miscalibration in autoregressive models and the forecast combination puzzle, highlighting its ability to solve analytically complex or computationally intensive time series problems. By allowing explicit control over decision-theoretic trade-offs, The Simulacrum offers analysts efficient, tailored estimation tools suited to their specific analytical goals.

item.title: Researchers introduce Bifocal Diffusion Language Models with asymmetric bidirectional context, achieving up to 12.9× throughput over bidirectional dLLMs and 2.9× speedup over autoregressive baselines in batch serving [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Bifocal Diffusion Language Models (dLLMs) that address a key challenge in language model design by combining asymmetric bidirectional context. Their approach, called R2LM (Right-to-Left Mamba), integrates standard causal attention for left-context with a lightweight reverse mechanism to provide compressed right-side context, enabling efficient parallel decoding with KV caching. This design achieves up to 12.9 times higher throughput than traditional bidirectional dLLMs and up to 2.9 times speedup over autoregressive baselines in batch serving, while maintaining or exceeding generation quality benchmarks. The team demonstrated these results through extensive experiments involving continued pretraining of the Qwen3-1.7B model on 60 billion tokens. R2LM effectively balances the trade-off between generation quality and inference efficiency by preserving cache compatibility and incorporating right-side context without performance loss. This innovation offers a promising direction for improving the speed and quality of language model inference in practical applications.

item.title: Researchers present KG2Cypher, a data-centric pipeline for building enterprise text-to-Cypher systems with LoRA-based inference, achieving over 95% exact match and 99.9% execution rate in Korean enterprise tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed KG2Cypher, a data-centric pipeline designed to create enterprise text-to-Cypher systems from existing knowledge graphs (KGs). This approach generates executable Cypher queries from graph facts and uses large language models (LLMs) to produce corresponding natural-language questions. The system then validates these pairs through LLM judgment and human review, converting them into candidate-aware supervised fine-tuning data. KG2Cypher incorporates class-conditioned schema prompting, entity retrieval, and LoRA-based inference to enhance performance. The pipeline was tested in Korean enterprise environments, where short search queries and schema variations pose challenges for language grounding. LoRA-based supervised fine-tuning significantly improved execution-result F1 scores, reaching 0.950 for broadcast-program queries and 0.92 for company queries. Overall, KG2Cypher achieved a 95.2% exact match rate, a 99.9% execution rate, and a 0.964 execution-result F1 score across an 11-class setting, demonstrating its effectiveness for building natural-language interfaces for private enterprise knowledge graphs.

item.title: Researchers propose Learning to Allocate (L2A), an end-to-end framework for resource-adaptive LLM inference that dynamically adjusts computation based on input and runtime resource budgets, achieving up to 34% layer sparsity with minimal accuracy loss on Llama-3-8B and Qwen-3-4B [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Learning to Allocate (L2A), an end-to-end framework designed for resource-adaptive inference in large language models (LLMs). Unlike traditional static models that use a fixed computational graph, L2A dynamically adjusts computation based on both the input and the available runtime resource budget. This approach integrates lightweight gating networks into LLMs to optimize task performance, logical consistency, and resource usage by selectively skipping layers, pruning heads, and reducing reasoning tokens according to real-time resource constraints. L2A was tested on Llama-3-8B and Qwen-3-4B models, achieving up to 34% layer sparsity while maintaining accuracy within 0.6% of dense baselines on benchmark tasks like GSM8K. This adaptive method outperforms static or heuristic baselines, which require separate tuning and suffer larger accuracy drops under similar inference times. By tracing the compute-accuracy trade-off frontier, L2A enables LLMs to maximize reasoning depth when resources allow and enforce efficiency when budgets tighten, making it well-suited for dynamic cloud environments with fluctuating resource availability.

item.title: Researchers propose Flexformer, a flexible linear Transformer with learnable attention kernels using trainable spectral frequencies, achieving improved efficiency and performance on long-sequence tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Flexformer, a flexible linear Transformer model that improves efficiency and performance on long-sequence tasks by learning attention kernels through trainable spectral frequencies. Unlike traditional Transformer models that face quadratic complexity and kernel-based linear attention methods that use fixed or weakly learnable kernels, Flexformer employs a fully data-driven approach to learn a wide range of attention kernels, including both stationary and more expressive nonstationary variants. Built on random Fourier feature-based linear attention, Flexformer demonstrates superior results in language modeling and sequence classification compared to baseline models. It can also be distilled from pretrained Transformers to replicate softmax attention and shows strong kernel transferability across different domains, making it a promising solution for scalable and effective long-sequence processing.

item.title: Researchers propose RS-Diffuser, a risk-sensitive offline diffusion planning framework using distributional value critics to improve safety and robustness in reinforcement learning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced RS-Diffuser, a risk-sensitive offline diffusion planning framework designed to enhance safety and robustness in reinforcement learning tasks. This approach integrates diffusion-based trajectory generation with distributional value critics to better account for rare but catastrophic outcomes, which are often overlooked by traditional risk-neutral diffusion planners. RS-Diffuser enables flexible behavior adjustment-risk-averse, risk-neutral, or risk-seeking-by modifying a risk parameter during inference without retraining the model. The framework includes a diffusion planner for future state trajectories, an inverse dynamics model for decoding actions, and a Monte Carlo distributional critic that estimates the full return distribution using quantile regression. During sampling, it applies risk-sensitive guidance based on tail-aware objectives like Conditional Value at Risk to steer trajectory generation toward desired risk profiles. Extensive testing on risk-sensitive benchmarks, including D4RL and robot navigation tasks, demonstrated that RS-Diffuser achieves state-of-the-art performance by improving overall returns and worst-case robustness while reducing safety violations.

item.title: Researchers propose Activation Amplification and Attenuation (A3), a lightweight module that improves neural network adversarial robustness by dynamically rescaling activations with minimal overhead [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Activation Amplification and Attenuation (A3), a lightweight module designed to enhance the adversarial robustness of neural networks by dynamically rescaling activations. A3 uses a learnable mask and scaling factor based on original activation magnitudes to amplify or attenuate signals, helping to mitigate the impact of adversarial perturbations with minimal changes to the network. The module operates by flipping the sign of the scaling operation to switch between amplification and attenuation modes, using amplified signals as negative references for new contrastive and ranking loss functions. Experiments show that training in amplification mode improves robustness in attenuation mode, and A3 achieves these benefits with few additional parameters and negligible computational overhead. The approach has been validated across various backbones, datasets, and training methods, consistently improving adversarial defense. The code is publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Study finds output-space allocation cost alignment improves accuracy but increases perplexity in calibration-guided compression of Qwen3-8B and shows minor effects on Llama-3.2-1B at lower compression ratios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study examines the impact of aligning allocation costs with output-space objectives in calibration-guided compression of large language models (LLMs). Using the ROCKET method on Qwen3-8B at 50% compression, the researchers found that output-space cost alignment improved average accuracy by 0.8 percentage points across eight zero-shot benchmarks but increased perplexity on WikiText by 16%, indicating a tradeoff between accuracy and perplexity. The study also observed a strong correlation between weight-space and output-space errors, which limited the divergence in allocation and resulted in modest overall effects. When applied to Llama-3.2-1B at 20% compression, the difference between using weight-space and output-space allocation costs was minimal, with nearly identical accuracy and perplexity results. This suggests that the choice of allocation cost function has a minor effect at lower compression ratios. The findings highlight that different allocation objectives may favor different downstream performance metrics, providing insights for optimizing training-free compression methods for LLMs.

item.title: Researchers introduce SHIFT, a gate-modulated activation steering framework to mitigate knowledge conflicts in retrieval-augmented generation by adaptively regulating LLM internal activations with under 0.01% trainable parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SHIFT, a new framework designed to address knowledge conflicts in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems by adaptively regulating internal activations of large language models (LLMs). SHIFT introduces a lightweight gate module that modulates neuron-level activations with fewer than 0.01% trainable parameters, allowing the backbone model to remain frozen while resolving conflicts between retrieved context and parametric knowledge during response generation. Unlike previous neuron-editing approaches that risk unintended effects on broader model functions, SHIFT's gate modulation enables LLMs to dynamically balance contextual and stored knowledge. Extensive testing across six datasets demonstrates SHIFT's effectiveness compared to existing methods, with all related datasets and code made publicly available for further research and development.

item.title: Researchers propose NLL-guided training-free method to select full-attention layers for sliding-window adaptation, achieving 64.6% accuracy with 25% full-attention layers on LongMemEval [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a training-free method called NLL-guided layer selection to optimize hybrid attention models that combine full and sliding-window attention for efficient long-context inference. This approach identifies which layers should retain full attention by measuring the negative log-likelihood degradation when switching layers from full to sliding-window attention. Tested on LongMemEval with the Qwen3-4B model, the method achieved 64.6% accuracy using only 25% of layers with full attention, matching the performance of a baseline using 50% full-attention layers while reducing computational costs by half. The NLL-guided selection outperformed existing periodic and LightTransfer-style baselines by significant margins, demonstrating that its effectiveness stems from addressing long-range attention needs rather than general layer sensitivity. The method requires only about 15 minutes of one-time calibration, offering a practical advancement in balancing efficiency and accuracy for deploying large language models with long-context capabilities.

item.title: Researchers find position bias correction insufficient to match iterative attention sorting in long-context language models, with single-pass debiasing closing only part of the accuracy gap [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated the effectiveness of position bias correction in long-context language models, which tend to underutilize information in middle positions. They proposed Debiased One-Pass Attention Sorting, a method that estimates and corrects position bias to enable single-pass document sorting. However, experiments on two models showed that this approach either matched uncorrected single-pass sorting or only partially closed the accuracy gap compared to iterative Attention Sorting, which reorders documents multiple times based on attention patterns.

item.title: Researchers present HPC-aware method for knowledge distillation that decouples teacher-student partitioning, achieving up to 67% higher samples-per-second than TRL on production HPC clusters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a high-performance computing (HPC)-aware method for knowledge distillation that decouples the partitioning of teacher and student models. This approach leverages the asymmetry between the larger teacher and smaller student models in terms of memory and communication needs, achieving up to 67% higher samples-per-second compared to the widely used TRL library on production HPC clusters. The method combines vertical and horizontal model partitioning and uses an analytical expression to identify optimal splitting strategies, avoiding unnecessary data structures for the teacher model. By exploiting topology-aware parallelism and the distinct characteristics of teacher and student models, this technique significantly accelerates knowledge distillation training in large-scale HPC environments.

item.title: Researchers develop parameter-efficient quantum-inspired fast weight programmers for multi-step traffic-matrix forecasting, outperforming LSTM models with reduced resource use [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed parameter-efficient quantum-inspired fast weight programmers to improve multi-step traffic-matrix forecasting, a critical task in network traffic engineering. These models, based on gated quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold network fast-weight programmers (QKAN-FWPs), predict future network demand more accurately and with fewer resources compared to traditional long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. The best-performing variant, G-QKANFWP, achieved the lowest root-mean-square error while using only about 22% of the resources of a larger LSTM model. The study evaluated three QKAN variants against matched-size and larger LSTM models under a fixed training budget, demonstrating that the quantum-inspired models outperform both classical LSTMs and gated fast-weight programmers. Analysis of convergence and channel-wise performance further confirmed the efficiency and accuracy advantages of the quantum-inspired approach. These findings suggest that combining classical slow programmers with quantum-inspired fast programmers offers a promising design for resource-conscious network traffic forecasting.

item.title: Researchers present Pepti-drift, a toxicity-aware framework generating antigen-specific peptides by attracting binding features and repelling toxicity in peptide embedding space [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Pepti-drift, a novel framework designed to generate antigen-specific peptides while minimizing toxicity. This approach uses a toxicity-aware latent refinement process that guides peptide candidates toward binding features specific to an antigen and away from regions associated with toxicity within a peptide embedding space. The method addresses the challenge that binding-promoting and toxicity-associated features often overlap in peptide representations. Pepti-drift employs a warm-up strategy to balance these competing objectives by initially focusing on attracting peptides with binding properties and subsequently increasing repulsion from toxic regions. This single antigen-conditioned drift step offers a promising advancement for therapeutic peptide discovery by improving specificity and safety in peptide design.

item.title: Researchers propose WattLayer, a task-independent layer-wise model estimating neural network inference energy with 19.6% median error across 295 architectures and 3 hardware platforms [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed WattLayer, a task-independent, layer-wise model designed to estimate the energy consumption of neural network inference with a median error of 19.6%. The model was tested on over 100,000 layers from 295 neural network architectures across three common AI tasks and three different hardware platforms, outperforming existing methods. WattLayer's layer-wise approach allows it to generalize to new tasks without requiring full retraining by leveraging shared layers across architectures. This methodology provides a standardized and precise tool for estimating AI inference energy consumption, addressing growing concerns about the environmental impact of AI. By enabling more accurate energy assessments, WattLayer offers valuable insights and practical support for designing energy-efficient AI systems across diverse applications and hardware configurations.

item.title: Researchers investigate activation-based memorization indicators to detect overfitting early during low-sample recalibration of sEMG deep learning decoders [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have explored the use of activation-based memorization indicators to detect overfitting early during the low-sample recalibration of deep learning models for surface electromyography (sEMG). Since collecting large datasets for subject-specific calibration is challenging, traditional overfitting detection methods are often impractical. The study demonstrates that monitoring activation statistics of neural network units during fine-tuning can reveal early signs of performance degradation without requiring additional validation data. The team conducted transfer learning experiments using a convolutional neural network pre-trained on multiple subjects and fine-tuned on individual users with limited repetitions.
