They observed that decreases in test accuracy corresponded with characteristic changes in activation rates of the network's last hidden layer. These findings suggest that activation-based memorization indicators offer a promising approach for identifying unsuccessful learning in low-sample sEMG calibration scenarios, potentially improving the reliability of personalized deep learning decoders.

item.title: Researchers propose GNBAN, a graph neural basis attention network for scalable, interpretable long-horizon demand forecasting across large retail entity sets, improving accuracy by 4-5% on major benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced GNBAN (Graph Neural Basis Attention Network), a novel architecture designed for scalable and interpretable long-horizon demand forecasting across extensive retail hierarchies. By representing retail data as a heterogeneous graph and decomposing forecasts into trend, seasonal, and generic components, GNBAN improves accuracy by 4-5% on major benchmarks like M5 Walmart and Favorita Grocery Sales compared to existing graph-based models. Its per-basis attention mechanism allows different basis functions to specialize in distinct temporal patterns while maintaining interpretability. GNBAN addresses challenges faced by traditional statistical and deep learning methods, which struggle with scalability and interpretability when forecasting thousands of correlated time series. The model's design enables a single system to serve an entire product catalog by leveraging relational data structures and an interpretable basis-decomposition head. Qualitative analysis confirms that the model effectively exposes underlying demand drivers without requiring additional explanation methods. These findings demonstrate that combining scalable relational forecasting with interpretable decomposition is feasible within a unified graph-based framework, offering promising advancements for demand forecasting in large retail settings.

item.title: Researchers study temporal fusion strategies for named entity recognition in historical French and German texts, finding late fusion methods improve robustness and temporal generalization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated how to improve named entity recognition (NER) in historical French and German texts by incorporating temporal metadata into language models. They explored various lightweight fusion strategies, including early and late fusion methods, to embed both absolute and relative temporal information into Transformer-based architectures. Their study found that late fusion techniques, such as cross-attention and adapters, enhance the robustness and temporal generalization of NER models, especially in earlier and noisier historical periods. The research addresses the challenge of temporal variation in historical texts, where entity forms and prominence change over time, complicating NER tasks. By systematically comparing fusion strategies on historical datasets, the study demonstrates that integrating temporal context at later stages of the model yields better performance than early fusion approaches. This work contributes to advancing natural language processing methods for diachronic text analysis and improving the handling of temporal dynamics in historical document processing.

item.title: Researchers extend Werewolf game with a Jester role to test multi-hop theory of mind in LLMs, finding Jester wins 60-70% of games across GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Llama-3.3-70B [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have enhanced the classic Werewolf social deduction game by introducing a Jester role, creating a triadic incentive structure to better evaluate multi-hop theory of mind in large language models (LLMs). Unlike traditional dyadic games where cues point to a single hidden side, the Jester wins by being voted out, requiring models to reason across three opposing utility functions. Testing this setup on GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Llama-3.3-70B showed the Jester winning 60-70% of games, while Werewolves rarely exceeded 20%, highlighting complex multi-agent reasoning challenges for LLMs. The study found that GPT-4.1 often made self-defeating moves by voting out the Jester early, whereas DeepSeek demonstrated a nuanced strategy of appearing suspicious without intentional suspicion, benefiting most from self-learning. These results suggest that triadic games reveal layers of strategic reasoning that simpler dyadic games fail to expose, offering a more rigorous test of theory-of-mind capabilities in language models.

item.title: Researchers propose two-stage fine-tuning with reinforcement learning to generate protein sequences matching targeted amino-acid compositions while preserving sequence quality [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a two-stage fine-tuning approach combining domain-adaptive fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to generate protein sequences that match specific amino-acid composition targets while maintaining sequence quality and diversity. This method addresses the challenge of steering protein language models toward explicit distributional design goals, particularly relevant for synthetic feed protein design where amino-acid composition affects nutritional value. The proposed pipeline first fine-tunes a protein language model on an in-domain dataset, then applies iterative reward-weighted fine-tuning via reinforcement learning anchored to the initial model. Evaluations on two amino-acid compositions show that fine-tuning alone brings sequences close to the target composition, while reinforcement learning enforces additional sequence constraints. The study also compares different reward designs and training stages, confirming that the approach achieves composition alignment without compromising sequence plausibility.

item.title: Researchers propose a multi-stage explainable framework using LLaMA-3.1 and SHAP to interpret speech-based cognitive impairment detection models with 72.11% F1 on NIA PREPARE benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-stage explainability framework that enhances the interpretability of transformer-based models used for speech-based cognitive impairment detection. This framework integrates SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for token attribution, theory-informed linguistic features, and a four-stage reasoning pipeline using LLaMA-3.1-70B-Instruct. It builds on the SpeechCARE-Adaptive Gating Network model, achieving an F1 score of 72.11% on the NIA PREPARE benchmark, and translates model outputs into four cognitive-linguistic dimensions such as lexical richness and semantic coherence. Physician evaluations on 70 stratified English samples showed strong alignment between the framework's explanations and patient cognitive profiles. Additionally, the framework received a System Usability Scale score of 82 out of 100, indicating its potential for integration into clinical workflows to provide noninvasive and accessible cognitive impairment screening.

item.title: Researchers introduce a synthetic multimodal NLP pipeline combining dialogue transcripts, audio analysis, and rule-based scoring to detect insurance fraud at first notice of loss [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a synthetic multimodal natural language processing pipeline designed to detect insurance fraud at the first notice of loss (FNOL). This approach integrates agent-customer dialogue transcripts, audio analysis, and rule-based scoring to identify indicators such as narrative reuse, structural inconsistencies, and repeated voices across cases. The system combines automatic speech recognition, speaker diarisation, named entity recognition, regex-based feature extraction, and large language model retrieval to generate a risk score that balances sensitivity with false positives. The framework replicates FNOL conditions by generating two-speaker audio and dialogue data, enabling comprehensive evaluation beyond text-only methods. Validation of the dataset and individual components demonstrates the pipeline's stability and potential for transfer to real-world applications, providing a reproducible baseline for multimodal insurance fraud detection.

item.title: Researchers introduce MLVC, a multi-platform neural video codec achieving real-time 100 FPS performance and over 70% BD-rate improvement on VCD benchmark across Apple, Intel, and Qualcomm NPUs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MLVC, a multi-platform neural video codec that achieves real-time encoding and decoding at 100 frames per second on common NPUs from Apple, Intel, and Qualcomm. MLVC addresses the challenges of cross-platform incompatibility and high computational costs seen in previous neural codecs by explicitly transmitting scale parameters to ensure consistent entropy coding across devices. This approach avoids decoding failures without requiring bit-exact arithmetic, enabling robust deployment across diverse hardware. Despite a slight increase in bitrate overhead, MLVC recovers coding efficiency through architectural enhancements such as gated memory, ReGLU activation, a long-term reference recovery mechanism, and domain-specific perceptual training. On the VCD video conferencing benchmark, it delivers over 70% BD-rate improvement compared to hardware HEVC, the strongest deployable baseline, while maintaining subjective quality comparable to DCVC-RT, which lacks cross-platform support. MLVC is the first neural video codec to combine competitive compression performance, real-time speed, and hardware robustness across multiple consumer platforms, making it suitable for widespread practical use. The researchers plan to release the code to facilitate adoption and further development.

item.title: Researchers present DG^VoiC, a speaker clustering framework for fraud investigation using anonymized real call-centre audio, achieving up to 99% accuracy in identifying repeated speakers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DG^VoiC, a speaker clustering framework designed to aid fraud investigations by analyzing anonymized call-centre audio. This system identifies repeated speakers across calls, a method that has been underutilized in fraud detection, achieving up to 99% accuracy in linking voices under real telephony conditions. The framework integrates anonymization aligned with sensitive information, speech-focused preprocessing, and cosine similarity-based clustering to verify speaker consistency and detect repeated voices among customers. The approach was tested on 121 recordings, with a subset of 56 samples grouped into 22 speaker clusters agreed upon by human evaluators. The best-performing configuration demonstrated high metrics including 96% Adjusted Mutual Information, 95% Adjusted Rand Index, and 100% homogeneity, indicating strong clustering performance. These results suggest that speaker clustering can provide a valuable additional signal for fraud analysts, enhancing verification processes and improving detection of fraudulent activity in call-centre workflows.

item.title: Researchers find large language models generate more accurate answers than self-evaluate on three of four in-context QA benchmarks, challenging assumptions in self-evaluation pipelines [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that large language models (LLMs) generate more accurate answers than they do when self-evaluating on three out of four in-context question-answering benchmarks, challenging the common assumption that evaluation is easier than generation. The study tested this in a controlled setting where the model judges its own generated answer based solely on a given context passage, eliminating external knowledge influences. The exception was the multi-hop MuSiQue benchmark, where self-evaluation performed better. Analysis revealed that during evaluation, models pay significantly less attention to the context and barely review the candidate answer compared to the generation phase. Further experiments using LoRA fine-tuning showed that this asymmetry is not due to training artifacts: fine-tuning for generation led to over-acceptance of answers, while fine-tuning for evaluation degraded generation performance. These findings question key assumptions underlying self-evaluation pipelines in language models.

item.title: Researchers demonstrate Large Language Models outperform traditional methods in single-truth and multi-truth data fusion tasks on benchmark datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that Large Language Models (LLMs) outperform traditional unsupervised truth discovery methods in data fusion tasks, which involve determining the correct values for object attributes from conflicting sources. Their study covers both single-truth scenarios, where only one correct value exists, and multi-truth scenarios, where multiple values may be valid. The evaluation was conducted using various prompting strategies on three benchmark datasets, showing consistent superiority of LLM-based approaches over methods like DART and LTM. The research explored domain-dependent and domain-independent prompts, including zero-shot and one-shot techniques, to assess LLM performance in tabular data fusion. The findings suggest that LLMs can effectively handle complex data integration challenges across different contexts. The authors have made their code publicly available on GitHub to support further research and application in this area.

item.title: Researchers introduce OperatorSHAP, a grid-agnostic method for fast and accurate Shapley value estimation in neural operators, enabling consistent attributions across irregular grids and resolutions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed OperatorSHAP, a novel grid-agnostic method for efficiently estimating Shapley values in neural operators, which are crucial for interpreting model predictions in physical applications like structural load assessment and weather forecasting. This approach overcomes limitations of existing methods that require homogeneous inputs, enabling consistent and accurate attributions across irregular grids and varying resolutions without retraining. OperatorSHAP introduces a training procedure similar to FastSHAP but extends its applicability to neural operators handling irregular data. The method is grounded in a theoretical framework connecting attributions in function space to Aumann-Shapley values, ensuring that its explanations align with state-of-the-art discrete Shapley values and transfer effectively across different grid sizes.

item.title: Researchers propose ADC-GNN, a diffusion-guided graph neural network for few-shot fraud detection, showing improved performance on public benchmarks and a telecom dataset with 1% training data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ADC-GNN, an Attention-guided Diffusion-Contrastive Graph Neural Network designed to improve few-shot fraud detection in graph-based transaction systems. This approach addresses challenges of sparse and imbalanced supervision and representation dilution by combining diffusion-guided feature augmentation, contrastive learning, and multi-hop spectral attention. ADC-GNN stabilizes node representations through noise-perturbed feature views and adaptively highlights fraud-relevant cues, enhancing detection accuracy with limited labeled data. The model was evaluated on three public benchmarks and a proprietary telecom transaction dataset with about 60,000 records. Under a 1% training data setting, ADC-GNN consistently outperformed existing graph fraud detection baselines. Additional analyses explored its stability, training ratios, and resource consumption, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency for real-world fraud detection scenarios.

item.title: Researchers propose CPAgents framework to generate interpretable composite cardiac phenotypes, improving disease association accuracy across nine clinical categories in population-scale imaging study [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CPAgents, a novel framework designed to generate interpretable composite cardiac phenotypes from imaging data, enhancing the accuracy of disease association studies across nine clinical categories. This system integrates three specialized agents that identify statistical issues, propose medically and statistically sound phenotype expressions, and verify these candidates through rigorous evaluation, producing transparent evidence trails for each accepted phenotype. Tested on a large cardiac imaging cohort, CPAgents outperformed traditional methods in disease discrimination, achieving top rankings in the majority of classifier-disease-metric combinations examined. The CPAgents framework addresses limitations of current phenome-wide association studies, which often rely on predefined single-variable phenotypes or expert-crafted features that may miss complex non-linear effects and interactions. By automatically constructing composite phenotypes such as polynomial, ratio, and interaction forms, the system enables scalable discovery of stronger and clinically interpretable phenotype-disease associations beyond expert-driven feature selection. This advancement holds promise for improving risk stratification and cardiovascular research at the population scale.

item.title: Researchers propose LLawCo framework to improve cooperation and task success in embodied multi-agent systems using learned behavioral laws and fine-tuned large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced LLawCo, a new framework designed to enhance cooperation and task success among embodied multi-agent systems by learning and applying behavioral laws. This approach enables agents to reflect on past failures, identify misaligned behaviors, and incorporate high-level cooperation principles like "Talk when necessary" and "Wait for partner" into their decision-making processes through supervised fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). To validate LLawCo, the team developed PARTNR-Dialog, a large-scale benchmark for multi-agent communication and cooperative planning. Experiments on this benchmark and existing tasks showed that LLawCo significantly improves cooperative efficiency and task success rates, achieving average success rate increases of 4.5% on PARTNR-Dialog and 6.8% on the TDW-MAT benchmark compared to leading open-source communicative agent frameworks across four different LLMs. These results suggest that explicitly learning and integrating behavioral laws can better align agents' actions with both their partners and task objectives, potentially advancing the development of more effective multi-agent systems in decentralized and partially observable environments.

item.title: Study analyzes 32 years of Sri Lankan remittances using machine learning, finds external macroeconomic factors drive inflows and projects 2026 remittances at USD 9 billion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing 32 years of Sri Lankan migration and remittance data from 1994 to 2025 uses machine learning and time-series modeling to identify key drivers of remittance inflows. The research finds that external macroeconomic factors, particularly exchange rate fluctuations and global oil prices, have a stronger influence on remittances than domestic economic indicators. The study's predictive models, especially Ridge Regression, outperform traditional methods and project remittances to reach approximately USD 9 billion by 2026 under stable conditions. The analysis employs a comprehensive 384-month dataset and applies techniques such as exploratory data analysis, stationarity corrections, and impulse response analysis to confirm the asymmetric effects of currency depreciation and oil price shocks. These findings underscore the structural dependence of Sri Lankan remittances on global economic conditions and highlight the importance of robust exchange rate policies, skilled migration strategies, and formal financial channels to support the country's economic resilience.

item.title: Researchers propose a framework for value-constrained reward allocation in fully delegated AI cooperatives using traversal learning for decentralized gradient attribution [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a framework for allocating rewards in fully delegated AI cooperatives, where human participants are represented by agents contributing data and model updates under diverse value constraints. The approach credits only those updates that meet each principal's value profile, using value-conditioned gradient filtering and online marginal contribution signals within a traversal learning (TL) system. TL enables decentralized backpropagation without the quality loss typical of aggregation-based distributed learning and provides more precise attribution than traditional federated learning methods by preserving explicit traversal and gradient paths. This framework addresses challenges in data valuation, federated contribution estimation, personalized federated learning, and pluralistic alignment by integrating cumulative revenue settlement mechanisms. The use of traversal learning offers a novel substrate for decentralized credit assignment, potentially improving fairness and efficiency in AI cooperative reward distribution.
